title: Sampling Temperature
shortDefinition: An LLM API setting that controls how random or deterministic the model's output is, affecting creativity vs. consistency.
definition: Sampling temperature is an LLM API setting that controls how random or deterministic the model's output generation is — a low temperature (close to 0) makes the model more consistently select the highest-probability next token, producing more focused, predictable, and repeatable output, while a higher temperature introduces more randomness, producing more varied and creative but less consistent output. Choosing the right temperature setting for your specific use case meaningfully affects whether your application's output is appropriately consistent or appropriately creative.

sections.title: How temperature affects output behavior
sections.description: Low temperature produces consistent output; high temperature produces creative variation.

content.text: At low temperature settings, the model consistently selects the token it considers most probable at each step, making output highly predictable and largely repeatable for the same input — well-suited to tasks requiring consistency, like structured data extraction, factual question-answering, or code generation where you want the same input to reliably produce similar output. At higher temperature settings, the model samples more probabilistically from a wider range of plausible tokens, producing more varied, creative output that can differ noticeably across multiple runs with the identical input — well-suited to creative writing, brainstorming, or content generation where variety is genuinely desirable.

items: Low temperature — consistent, predictable, repeatable output.
High temperature — varied, creative, less consistent output.
Consistency tasks — data extraction, QA, code generation.
Creative tasks — writing, brainstorming, content generation.
No universal setting — depends on your specific use case.

content.title: The key insight
content.text: Low temperature for consistency, high temperature for creativity — choosing the right setting depends entirely on what your application needs.

sections.title: Choosing the right temperature for your use case

content.text: There's no universally 'correct' temperature setting — the right choice depends entirely on whether your application values consistency or creative variety more. Data extraction, classification, and any task feeding into downstream automated systems generally benefit from low temperature settings to ensure reliable, repeatable output. Creative writing assistance, brainstorming tools, and conversational applications where some response variety improves user experience generally benefit from moderate-to-higher temperature settings, though excessively high settings can produce output that's too erratic or incoherent to be useful.

items: Low temperature — data extraction, classification, automated systems.
Moderate temperature — conversational applications, balanced use cases.
Higher temperature — creative writing, brainstorming, content variety.
Excessively high — can produce erratic or incoherent output.
Test and validate — the right value depends on your specific use case.

sections.title: Limitations and risks of temperature configuration

content.text: Temperature configuration has limitations. Temperature doesn't guarantee perfect determinism even at low settings due to provider-specific variations. Different providers implement temperature differently, so settings are not directly comparable across providers. Temperature interacts with other sampling parameters (like top-p), and the right setting is use-case dependent and may require testing to determine. Overly low temperature can make outputs mechanical or repetitive, while overly high temperature can produce incoherent responses. Temperature doesn't affect model quality or capability — it only controls output characteristics.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions about sampling temperature

items.question: What temperature setting should I use for data extraction tasks?
items.answer: Generally a low temperature (close to 0), since data extraction benefits from consistent, repeatable output for the same input, rather than creative variation.

items.question: What temperature setting is best for creative content generation?
items.answer: Generally a moderate-to-higher temperature, since some output variety is often desirable for creative tasks, though the right specific value depends on testing against your specific use case's quality requirements.

items.question: Can different parts of the same application use different temperature settings?
items.answer: Yes, this is common and often appropriate — ClickMasters configures temperature per LLM call based on that specific call's purpose within a larger pipeline.

items.question: Does temperature affect how fast the LLM generates a response?
items.answer: Generally not significantly — temperature primarily affects output randomness/creativity, not generation speed, which is more affected by output length and model size.

items.question: How long does temperature and output configuration tuning take?
items.answer: 4–10 weeks depending on whether it's tuning a single existing feature or configuring multiple distinct calls within a larger pipeline.

items.question: Is temperature the only setting that affects LLM output variability?
items.answer: No, other parameters (like top-p sampling) also affect output randomness; ClickMasters configures the full relevant parameter set appropriately for your specific use case, not just temperature alone.

items.question: What is the difference between temperature and top-p sampling?
items.answer: Temperature controls the randomness of token selection by shaping the probability distribution. Top-p sampling (nucleus sampling) limits the selection to the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds p. Both affect output randomness and are often used together.

items.question: Does temperature 0 mean the same output every time?
items.answer: Temperature 0 makes the model choose the most probable token at each step, producing highly consistent output. However, due to floating-point variations and other factors, outputs may still have minor differences across runs in practice.

items.question: What is the typical temperature range for LLMs?
items.answer: Most LLMs support temperatures from 0 to 2.0 or higher. Values between 0 and 1 are most common — low (0.1-0.3) for consistency, medium (0.5-0.7) for balanced, and high (0.8-1.2) for creativity.

items.question: Can temperature be set differently for different users or sessions?
items.answer: Yes — temperature is a per-request setting that can be configured based on user preferences, session context, or the specific use case. This allows different users to have different output characteristics.
